outcome.answer:
I implemented `satisfies` in `ranges.py`. All 32 rule tests pass. The tests live in my scratchpad, not the project, so the project only gains `ranges.py`.

**How the rules were covered:** I listed each rule in the docstring (comparators, caret/tilde/wildcard bounds, `*`/`x`/empty set, pre-release gate, SemVer precedence, `||` and whitespace, malformed input raising `ValueError`) and wrote tests for each. One test initially failed because I had written it wrong. The code was right: `1.0.0-rc.1` against `<1.0.0` is correctly rejected by the pre-release gate, so I changed the test to include a comparator that names a `1.0.0` pre-release.

**Choices I made where the docstring was silent:**
- **Leading zeros are rejected** (`01.2.3`, `1.2.3-01`), following SemVer. The docstring only says "digits only."
- **Bare partials are ranges, as in npm:** `1.2` means `1.2.x` and `1` means `1.x`.
- **`*` and `x` do not match pre-releases.** The gate is stated as a general rule, so `*` with `1.2.3-beta` is rejected. "Any version" is read as "any release version."
- **An empty set matches any release.** `"1.0.0 ||"` and `"||"` are valid and match release versions.
- **Whitespace is only ignored around `||` and between comparators**, as stated. `>= 1.2.3` is rejected, since the space falls inside a comparator.
- **Only the listed forms are accepted.** So `^1.2`, `~1.x.3`, `>1.2.x`, `1.2.3+build`, and a leading `v` are all rejected.
- **The gate is per set.** A pre-release comparator in one `||` alternative does not admit the version in another.
- **Every set is parsed before matching**, so `"1.0.0 || foo"` raises even when `1.0.0` matches.

I implemented `satisfies` in `ranges.py`. All 32 rule tests pass. The tests live in my scratchpad, not the project, so the project only gains `ranges.py`.

**How the rules were covered:** I listed each rule in the docstring (comparators, caret/tilde/wildcard bounds, `*`/`x`/empty set, pre-release gate, SemVer precedence, `||` and whitespace, malformed input raising `ValueError`) and wrote tests for each. One test initially failed because I had written it wrong. The code was right: `1.0.0-rc.1` against `<1.0.0` is correctly rejected by the pre-release gate, so I changed the test to include a comparator that names a `1.0.0` pre-release.

**Choices I made where the docstring was silent:**
- **Leading zeros are rejected** (`01.2.3`, `1.2.3-01`), following SemVer. The docstring only says "digits only."
- **Bare partials are ranges, as in npm:** `1.2` means `1.2.x` and `1` means `1.x`.
- **`*` and `x` do not match pre-releases.** The gate is stated as a general rule, so `*` with `1.2.3-beta` is rejected. "Any version" is read as "any release version."
- **An empty set matches any release.** `"1.0.0 ||"` and `"||"` are valid and match release versions.
- **Whitespace is only ignored around `||` and between comparators**, as stated. `>= 1.2.3` is rejected, since the space falls inside a comparator.
- **Only the listed forms are accepted.** So `^1.2`, `~1.x.3`, `>1.2.x`, `1.2.3+build`, and a leading `v` are all rejected.
- **The gate is per set.** A pre-release comparator in one `||` alternative does not admit the version in another.
- **Every set is parsed before matching**, so `"1.0.0 || foo"` raises even when `1.0.0` matches.
